title: TCP SYN and FIN each occupy a sequence number
summary: The sequence number is advanced by data bytes, with SYN occupying a position before the data and FIN after the data.
applies: Packet capture and reconstruction; TCP sequence space
aliases: Confirmation number is off by one
detail: When the SYN sequence number is 100 and there is no data, the acknowledgment number after the peer receives it can be 101. Simple ACK does not occupy an additional number.
boundary: SYN or FIN may also carry data, and the actual data length must still be taken into account when calculating the next sequence number.
relevance: When checking offline TCP streams, explain sequence number increments that occur even though not a single byte of data is applied.
